items.impact: The visible tabs, theme selector, file-search controls, and file-tree examples cannot certify product navigation, interaction, or accessibility by themselves.
items.statement: Every control in this window is retained as owner-adjudicated concept/source-lineage input, including controls with recorded accessibility candidates, and none is promoted as production evidence.

items.statement: The replace-all control is promoted to production-wiring-required with a canonical command, handler, state selector, disabled-reason selector, accessibility contract, and an implementation-certification evidence checklist.

evidence.exact_quote: "receipt_or_event_effect": "route/projection receipt or explicit no-persist UI effect",

items.impact: Implementers may choose incompatible persistence, receipt, atomicity, partial-success, and rollback behavior for a multi-file mutation while still appearing to satisfy the generic row.
items.statement: The replace-all wiring row permits either a route/projection receipt or a no-persist UI effect and does not define atomicity, partial-failure reporting, retry safety, undo, rollback, or a falsifiable receipt payload.
items.title: Replace-all outcome and recovery semantics are left open

items.impact: Search scope changes, result-group focus, and result opening have canonical dispatch and visible disabled-reason obligations rather than relying on inline mock handlers.
items.statement: The window promotes search scope, result-group focus, and result opening to canonical command wiring with handler, enabled-state, disabled-reason, accessibility, and evidence requirements.
items.title: Search scope and result navigation are production-wiring candidates

"test_evidence": "production render/control, dispatcher, disabled-reason, receipt/event, accessibility, and regression evidence required before implementation certification"

items.impact: A result can become stale after edits, rename, deletion, or concurrent search refresh; without a defined response the GUI may open the wrong location, silently fail, or present obsolete state as current.
items.statement: The open-result contract does not specify target identity/versioning, behavior for deleted or moved files, out-of-range positions, concurrent index refresh, user feedback, or a precise failure oracle.
items.title: Stale search-result behavior is unspecified

items.impact: Selected replacement, global replacement, and previous/next traversal are bound to canonical commands and production enablement/accessibility evidence requirements.
items.statement: The window defines production wiring envelopes for replace-selected, replace-all, previous-result, and next-result, while retaining the debugger start control as concept-only.
items.title: Search mutation and traversal commands are separated from concept-only debugging

evidence.exact_quote: "receipt_or_event_effect": "route/projection receipt or explicit no-persist UI effect",

items.impact: Replace-all can alter multiple files without a specified confirmation threshold, transaction boundary, conflict behavior, audit payload, or recovery path, risking silent partial edits and misleading success UI.
items.statement: The repeated replace-all wiring contract still does not define preflight, confirmation, atomicity, per-file failures, cancellation, concurrent edits, undo/rollback, or exact receipt contents.
items.title: Multi-file replacement lacks destructive-action safety semantics

evidence.exact_quote: "owner_rationale": "Owner-adjudicated as concept/source-lineage only. This control is not production evidence and is not promoted until a canonical owner doc accepts the behavior and a production wiring row supplies command/state/receipt/test evidence."

items.impact: Worktree filters, expansion rows, diff, merge, stash, and remove demonstrations cannot grant source-control authority or certify destructive behavior.
items.statement: The worktree-status and action controls are uniformly owner-adjudicated concept/source-lineage artifacts even where the mock UI exposes merge, stash, or removal actions.
items.title: Worktree action mocks remain non-authoritative

items.impact: Staged and unstaged diff controls normalize the concept alias to one canonical command and bind source-control actions to handler, state, disabled reason, event, accessibility, and test evidence.
items.statement: The source-control window normalizes cmd.git.open_diff to cmd.git.diff_open and gives diff-open, unstage-hunks, and discard-hunks explicit production wiring rows.
items.title: Git diff and hunk actions have canonical wiring identities

items.impact: Discard could target the wrong or stale hunks, erase uncommitted work without a required confirmation or recovery path, and emit an event too generic to prove what changed.
items.statement: The discard-hunks production row names dispatch and a generic command-applied event but does not require target identity/version checks, confirmation, cancellation, partial-failure behavior, recovery, or event fields proving the discarded scope.
items.title: Discard-hunks lacks irreversible-action safeguards

items.impact: Assistive technology may announce only an ambiguous multiplication/cross glyph for a destructive command; the same pattern gives unstage only a minus glyph, weakening localization and action clarity.
items.statement: The production accessibility contract copies the symbol-only visual labels as accessible names even though the source attributes provide semantic titles such as Discard and Unstage.
items.title: Symbol-only Git actions have misleading accessible names

segments.summary: Verified the inventory's source-lineage boundary, summary accounting, retired launch authorities, compatibility aliases, and false-positive exclusion.
Reviewed initial page, theme, file-search, and file-tree controls and confirmed their owner-adjudicated concept-only status and recorded accessibility candidates.
Reviewed file context-menu mutation, clipboard, chat, and terminal mock commands and confirmed their fixture quarantine and explicit acceptance ineligibility.
Reviewed open-with and local-save fixtures plus the production replace-all row; identified its unresolved receipt, atomicity, partial-failure, and recovery choices.
Reviewed search scope, result-group focus, and result-opening contracts and found stale-target and concurrent-refresh behavior absent from the production envelope.
Reviewed remaining result controls, selected/global replacement, result traversal, and the concept-only debugger control; found multi-file mutation safety and recovery undefined.
Reviewed debugger summaries and worktree filters, rows, diff, merge, stash, and remove actions and confirmed that none carries production authority.
Reviewed worktree/source-control concepts and production diff, unstage, and discard rows; identified missing discard safeguards and symbol-only accessible-name defects.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner document fixes transaction, receipt, retry, partial-failure, and rollback semantics for search replacement commands?
Which canonical source-control contract fixes target identity, confirmation, recovery, and receipt payload requirements for discard-hunks?
Where are production accessible names for symbol-only Git actions required to use localized semantic action labels rather than glyphs?
